requirement_text.REQ-149: Design requirement settling OQ-1: how a Lua script execution gets a configurable memory limit. Deliverable: lib/letflow/design/req149-lua-memory-limit.md naming one RECOMMENDED MECHANISM, stating which of LUA-09's two clauses it satisfies, rejecting :max_instructions, and disposing of the decision 0014 addendum question.

task.description:
Validate CODE-DESIGNER's artefact at lib/letflow/design/req149-lua-memory-limit.md on branch feature/WF02-REQ149-20260826. Check out the feature branch before reading.

Gate criteria:
1. Every acceptance criterion from REQ-149 is covered by the artefact:
   - Names exactly one RECOMMENDED MECHANISM (not a pros/cons list)
   - Quotes a real search of deps/lua/ source (not just docs) for memory-limit options
   - For :max_heap_size candidate, quotes a real run showing what happens when exceeded
   - States explicitly which of LUA-09's two clauses are satisfied and which are not
   - Explicitly rejects :max_instructions as a memory proxy with decision 0014 OQ-1 citation
   - States whether a decision 0014 addendum is needed (and if so, writes it)
   - No lib/letflow/engine/ file and no mix.exs change made
2. No implementation code present (this is a design-only requirement)
3. The design is unambiguous enough for REQ-156 to implement against
acceptance_criteria: All six REQ-149 acceptance criteria are verified against the actual artefact
PASS only if all six are met
FAIL with specific missing coverage if any criterion fails

criteria.1_single_recommended_mechanism: PASS — Section 3 names exactly one mechanism: ':max_heap_size with kill: true' (Candidate A).
criteria.2_real_source_search: PASS — Section 1 documents that deps/lua/ is absent (commit 984bbc9, AC5 guardrail); cites REQ-148 spike doc with explicit grep commands and file paths (deps/lua/lib/lua.ex, deps/lua/lib/lua/api.ex, deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/state.ex); no memory/heap/limit/alloc pattern found in source.
criteria.3_max_heap_size_empirical_run: PASS — Section 2 Candidate A quotes scratch/lua_memory_spike.exs run, actual output: 'EXIT REASON (max_heap_size): :killed'.
criteria.4_lua09_clauses: PASS — Section 3 table: 'terminate the script' = YES (empirical evidence), 'fail gracefully' = NO (no allocator hook, BEAM kills process before Lua can observe error). Both clauses explicitly addressed.
criteria.5_max_instructions_rejection: PASS — Section 4 explicitly: ':max_instructions MUST NOT be used as a proxy for a memory limit.' Cites Decision 0014 OQ-1: 'unsound — allocation is not proportional to instruction count'. String-in-single-instruction counter-example given.
criteria.6_decision_0014_addendum: PASS — Section 5 states 'Addendum to 0014 is NOT required. OQ-1 is resolved by this design document.' Reasoning provided: 0014 already anticipated this outcome.

structural_checks.no_engine_files: PASS — git diff --stat main...HEAD shows only lib/letflow/design/req149-lua-memory-limit.md (312 insertions, 0 other files).
structural_checks.no_implementation_code: PASS — spike scripts quoted as evidence in design doc; no .ex files created in lib/letflow/.

result.implementability: PASS — REQ-156 has sufficient specification: max_heap_words config key, nil handling, spawn_opt call shape, {:error, :memory_limit_exceeded} signal mapping.
